markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize **recent-prefix training with moderate lexical negatives**, tested through staged controls. Preserve one BERT4Rec per category. This remains a hypothesis; supplied diagnostics establish weaknesses, not validation gains.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Broad matches displace specific choices; discrimination needs improvement, but compatibility labels are unavailable. (2) Historical interests obscure current priorities; recent targets provide observable supervision, not evidence of mood. (3) Industrial and Electronics have wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%; negative lower-tail margins motivate discrimination, whereas embedding scores near 0.5 do not indicate collapse.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Terminal masking already appears in BERT4Rec [1]; additional exposure is an adaptation. (2) Recency sampling [2] motivates recent targets but establishes no optimal BERT4Rec distribution. (3) GenNi supports informative negatives, while DPR supports lexical mining in retrieval [4,5]; neither validates title-based BERT4Rec sampling. (4) SimANS and UFNRec motivate false-negative caution [6,7]; lexical similarity is neither model-score hardness nor proof of irrelevance.

The framework links **temporal alignment → prefix sampling**, **specificity → negative selection**, and **ranking reliability → controlled losses and paired validation**. Missing compatibility supervision remains a gap throughout.

Scores below are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a positive (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Increase terminal exposure [1,2] | 2/6/6/6/2 | Established mechanism; promising alignment; targets immediacy; tests terminal errors; simple sampler | Little novelty; uncertain transfer; weak specificity; training margins may not improve; padding needs care |
| B. Moderate title-confusable negatives [4–7] | 3/6/6/7/5 | Testable adaptation; reusable mining; targets broad matches; stresses discrimination; standard sparse tools | Existing mining principle; uncertain lexical signal; no compatibility guarantee; false negatives; exclusion/index complexity |
| C. Apply B to recent terminal prefixes [1,2,4–7] | 4/7/7/7/5 | Useful combination; extensible; addresses specificity and recency; targets weak margins; unchanged inference | Incremental novelty; gains unproven; intent remains latent; interacting changes; several controls required |

**Select C**, retaining A as its simpler fallback. It explicitly targets broad matches displacing specific choices and historical interests outweighing current priorities, plus weak lower-tail margins. It cannot establish equipment ownership, compatibility, or mood.

Keep ordinary Cloze training. Ramp terminal-prefix probability from 0.25 to 0.50; sample endpoints through a defined uniform/recency mixture, replace the target with MASK, and discard later interactions. Compare uniform terminal negatives against a 25% lexical mixture using identical normalized pairwise loss and counts. Lexical sampling never adds inference scores. Exact distributions, exclusions, fallbacks, and weights are specified below.

Ablate terminal alignment, recency, then lexical sampling separately. Pairwise versus CE is a separate loss comparison, not evidence for mining. Predeclare validation cadence and trial limits within 43,200 GPU-seconds. Select using fixed macro validation HR@10; report paired hit changes and conditional uncertainty [8–11], acknowledging adaptive-selection optimism. Preserve seeds, routing, limits, diagnostic interfaces, and checkpoint/predictor consistency. Left-padded inference reads the final MASK position, never nonpadding-count minus one.

idea.description: Train each category's single BERT4Rec with ordinary Cloze supervision plus a curriculum of recent terminal-prefix examples. Test whether replacing a modest fraction of uniform training negatives with reproducibly selected title-confusable candidates improves fixed macro validation HR@10.
idea.motivation: Address two observed user failures: broadly plausible recommendations displacing specific choices, and historical interests outweighing recent priorities. Target negative lower-tail positive–negative margins in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics. These mechanisms are indirect: lexical similarity does not reveal compatibility or current intent, and larger training margins do not establish validation gains. Embedding scores near 0.5 provide no basis for a collapse-removal objective.
idea.implementation_notes:
Architecture and data: retain the corrected host BERT4Rec backbone, reserved MASK, bidirectional masked-target learning, appended-mask inference, four-category routing, and one independently trained model/checkpoint per category. No independent predictors or inference fusion. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, supplied splits, single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs, and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Use only public training interactions and permitted titles/descriptions/timestamps. Do not use unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices, stores, simulator traits, hidden test files, external datasets, pretrained weights, or other trials' checkpoints.

Terminal construction: sample users uniformly among training histories of length n>=2. Use one-indexed endpoints t in {2,...,n}. Define r_beta(t)=exp[-beta*(n-t)/(n-2)]/Z for n>2 and the sole endpoint t=2 for n=2. Use p(t)=0.5/(n-1)+0.5*r_beta(t), beta=2; beta=0 is the uniform control. The visible sequence contains the last L-1 interactions strictly before t, followed by MASK, then left padding. Target x_t never appears in its target position; all later interactions are absent. Earlier genuine repeats may remain. Let q(epoch)=0.25+0.25*min(epoch/50,1), with epochs numbered from zero. Sample one task branch per batch: terminal with probability q, otherwise unchanged baseline random Cloze. Never feed shifted targets through a bidirectional visible sequence.

Lexical index: fit per-category word TF–IDF using available titles only, Unicode NFKC normalization, case folding, whitespace collapse, sklearn word unigrams/bigrams, token_pattern='(?u)\\b\\w\\w+\\b', min_df=2, sublinear_tf=True, norm='l2'. This uses permitted catalog metadata, without interaction labels beyond training. Construct exact sparse cosine neighborhoods in bounded blocks; avoid a dense catalog-by-catalog matrix. Sort positive-similarity neighbors by descending cosine, then ascending item ID. Remove normalized-title duplicates and cosine>=0.95 candidates as a proposed, unvalidated safeguard. Define the moderate pool as original sorted ranks 11–50 after duplicate removal. Then remove the target and all items in that user's observed training history, and renormalize uniformly over remaining pool members. Missing/empty titles or empty pools trigger uniform fallback. These numerical choices are fixed initial hypotheses, not literature-established thresholds. Log pool coverage, fallback frequency, lexical similarity, and detached model-score difficulty separately.

Sampling and objective: for each terminal target draw K=32 unique eligible negatives, or all eligible items if fewer exist. In C draw H=min(8,floor(K_actual/4)) uniformly without replacement from the eligible lexical pool, reducing H when necessary; draw K_actual-H uniformly without replacement from remaining eligible real items. If H=0 use uniform-only loss. Otherwise L_terminal=(1-alpha)*mean(softplus(s_random-s_positive))+alpha*mean(softplus(s_lexical-s_positive)), alpha=H/K_actual<=0.25. Thus sampling counts and branch loss weights are explicit; the lexical branch contributes at most 25% of loss weight, but individual loss values or gradients are not capped. Uniform controls use the mean pairwise loss over the same total negative count. If no eligible negatives exist, resample the example with a bounded retry policy and record skips. Keep the ordinary Cloze loss unchanged and record its exact reduction from the supplied baseline. Expected mixed loss is (1-q)*L_Cloze+q*L_terminal; alternate-branch training estimates this directly. Pairwise loss does not approximate full softmax, and no uniform LogQ correction is applied to mined candidates. Excluding all known training-history positives affects sampling only; later interactions are never exposed as model inputs or targets. Future unobserved positives remain a false-negative risk.

Controlled search: predeclare at most four configurations: baseline Cloze; uniform-endpoint terminal mixture with uniform pairwise negatives; recency-endpoint terminal mixture with uniform pairwise negatives; the same recency mixture with lexical negatives. The first comparison jointly changes terminal exposure and its objective, so it cannot isolate masking from loss. The second isolates endpoint recency; the third isolates lexical sampling conditional on the pairwise setup. A separate CE control is desirable only if budget remains: use full-catalog CE over real items, excluding PAD/MASK, on identical sampled terminal targets. Never attribute CE-versus-pairwise differences to negative mining. Keep backbone, optimizer, negative count, seeds, and planned training steps matched wherever applicable. Fix validation checks every 10 epochs, select the earliest checkpoint on exact macro-HR ties, log every look and GPU cost, and cap total GPU consumption at 43,200 seconds. Before launch estimate a common epoch cap <=200 that permits the planned comparisons; if insufficient, prioritize baseline, uniform terminal control, and recency control before lexical mining. Interrupted or unmatched runs are exploratory rather than clean matched-compute comparisons. Use a predeclared practical threshold of +0.005 absolute macro HR@10 as a descriptive selection threshold, not a significance guarantee. If C does not clear it versus its immediate uniform-negative control, prefer the simpler control. All selection uses validation only.

Evaluation and shortcut checks: retain identical 200 validation users/category, the pinned 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42, masking, history truncation, and tie handling. When host outputs expose per-user hits, report gained/lost hits and macro delta; bootstrap paired users within category 10,000 times with analysis seed 42 and equal category weights for a 95% percentile interval. Do not modify the evaluator to obtain unavailable outputs. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidate sets; they exclude seed/candidate uncertainty and do not correct winner optimism. Exact per-category McNemar tests or macro paired randomization are optional exploratory analyses, not additional selection criteria. Inspect paired ranks, margins, history-length strata, and text-coverage strata when available. Do not optimize lexical-overlap diagnostics or treat unidentified-item skips as rejection. Title resemblance can promote lexical shortcuts; the uniform control and unchanged evaluator test utility, while full-catalog recommendations for twenty training users remain qualitative and cannot establish population or benchmark performance. Preserve untouched final evaluation for host confirmation.

Compatibility: retain ModelView, view.model as the actual nn.Module, view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data interfaces. Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Adapt probes to genuinely masked target positions, never shifted visible targets. Freeze diagnostic samples, negative IDs, padding, masking, and tie rules across comparisons. Mark missing metadata attribution as unavailable. Read each left-padded sequence using max occupied position; appended MASK is normally at L-1. Serialize architecture configuration, reserved token IDs, item mapping, weights, and any required inference state through the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs exactly the selected single model. Lexical pools are training-only. No host baseline source is included in this prompt, so the algorithm below is reproducible pseudocode rather than a claimed drop-in train.py.
idea.pseudocode:
predeclare configurations, validation cadence, compute cap, tie rule, and selection threshold
for configuration in budget_feasible_predeclared_order:
    for category in four_categories:
        seed_training(42)
        model = initialize_corrected_host_BERT4Rec()
        lexical_pools = build_deterministic_title_TFIDF_pools_if_required()
        for epoch in range(common_epoch_cap_at_most_200):
            q = 0.25 + 0.25 * min(epoch / 50, 1)
            for batch_index in range(200):
                if configuration_uses_terminal and Bernoulli(q):
                    user = sample_uniform_eligible_training_user()
                    history = training_history(user)
                    t = sample_endpoint(history, beta=configuration_beta,
                                        uniform_mixture_weight=0.5)
                    target = history[t - 1]
                    preceding = history[:t - 1]
                    sequence = left_pad(preceding[-(L - 1):] + [MASK], L)
                    eligible = real_items_excluding(target, all_training_items(user))
                    negatives, branch_labels = sample_unique_negatives(
                        eligible, K=32, lexical_limit=8,
                        lexical_pool=lexical_pools[target] if enabled else None)
                    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
                    mask_position = max_index_where(sequence != PAD)
                    positive_score = model.predict_score(features[mask_position], target)
                    negative_scores = model.predict_score(features[mask_position], negatives)
                    loss = normalized_pairwise_branch_loss(
                        positive_score, negative_scores, branch_labels,
                        lexical_weight=lexical_count / total_negative_count)
                else:
                    sequence, masked_targets = unchanged_baseline_cloze_batch()
                    loss = unchanged_baseline_masked_target_loss(sequence, masked_targets)
                optimizer_step(loss)
            if (epoch + 1) % 10 == 0:
                request_unchanged_host_validation()
                log_all_validation_looks_and_GPU_cost()
                retain_single_checkpoint_using_predeclared_macro_HR_rule()
        export_exact_selected_model_with_matching_predictor_writer()
    compare_configuration_using_fixed_four_category_macro_HR_only()
    if available: report_paired_hit_changes_and_conditional_bootstrap_interval()
choose_simpler_control_unless_added_complexity_clears_predeclared_threshold()
never_select_using_hidden_test_results()

originality.positive: Combines recent terminal-prefix supervision with a precisely controlled lexical-negative experiment while retaining a single BERT4Rec and unchanged inference.
originality.negative: Terminal masking, recency sampling, lexical mining, and mixed negative objectives are existing techniques; the contribution is an incremental combination rather than a new model class.

future_potential.positive: Creates an interpretable sequence of controls for improving immediate-choice discrimination using only permitted histories and public text.
future_potential.negative: The previous score of 8 overstated evidence: sparse titles, lexical shortcuts, false negatives, and sampled-metric limitations may prevent useful generalization.

code_difficulty.positive: Keeps the trained backbone and inference architecture unchanged; modifications concentrate in training-example construction, sparse lexical indexing, and loss calculation.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient deterministic neighborhoods, exclusions, fallback handling, checkpoint consistency, and compute-controlled comparisons require substantial care. The original description understated specification gaps despite assigning a reasonable midrange difficulty.

related_work.title: [1] BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides bidirectional masked-item learning and appended-mask next-item inference.
Includes last-item-only masking to align training with next-item prediction.
limitations: Increasing terminal exposure adapts an existing mechanism.
Does not establish gains for this curriculum on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: [2] Recency-based Sampling of Sequences
contributions: Motivates emphasizing recent targets while retaining older-target supervision.
limitations: Transfer to BERT4Rec and the proposed endpoint distribution require validation.
Recency does not establish present need or mood.

related_work.title: [3] EMM (2026), as described in the supplied search results
contributions: Motivates controlled hard–random mixtures, ID exclusion, and similarity-window safeguards.
limitations: The supplied summary does not establish BERT4Rec or target-category gains.
Its safeguards do not validate the proposed lexical rank bands or remove false negatives.

related_work.title: [4] GenNi: Generative Negative Sampling for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Supports investigating informative negatives in sequential recommendation using current model preferences.
limitations: Model-defined difficulty differs from title overlap.
Does not directly validate the proposed lexical sampler.

related_work.title: [5] Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
contributions: Provides adjacent evidence for adding a BM25-selected negative in retrieval training.
limitations: Studies text retrieval rather than BERT4Rec recommendation.
Its retriever uses pretrained representations; only the lexical candidate-mining principle is relevant here.

related_work.title: [6] SimANS: Simple Ambiguous Negatives Sampling for Dense Text Retrieval
contributions: Motivates avoiding an exclusive focus on the highest-scoring negatives.
limitations: Its bands concern learned relevance scores, not lexical cosine similarity.
Does not establish transferable title thresholds or mixture weights.

related_work.title: [7] UFNRec
contributions: Documents the importance of false negatives in sequential recommendation.
limitations: Does not establish that moderate lexical similarity identifies true negatives.
Observed-history exclusions cannot remove unobserved future positives.

related_work.title: [8] Approximate Statistical Tests for Comparing Supervised Classification Learning Algorithms
contributions: Provides methodological context for paired outcome comparisons and McNemar testing.
limitations: User-level comparisons conditional on trained models do not quantify training-seed uncertainty.
Testing a selected winner does not remove adaptive-selection bias.

related_work.title: [9] Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides paired-bootstrap methodology transferable to paired validation-user outcomes.
limitations: The proposed within-category, equal-weight macro bootstrap is a task-specific adaptation.
Conditional bootstrap intervals do not correct repeated validation selection.

related_work.title: [10] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog model ordering.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned evaluator.
Fixed candidates improve comparison consistency without establishing full-catalog quality.

related_work.title: [11] On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains optimism introduced by repeated model selection.
limitations: Predeclared search limits reduce opportunities for overfitting but do not eliminate winner optimism.
Untouched final evaluation remains necessary for confirmation.
